newsitem.title: MEXICO: BASEBALL-ALL FOUR TEAMS 2-2 IN CARIBBEAN SERIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ALL FOUR TEAMS 2-2 IN CARIBBEAN SERIES.

text.p: The Caribbean Baseball Series was all tied up with all four teams having records of 2-2 in the six-day tournament after games Friday.

Former Major Leaguer Matt Stark drilled a pinch-hit home run to spark a dramatic ninth-inning comeback and lead Mexico, represented by Culiacan Tomato Growers, to a 6-5 victory over Venezuela's Magellan Navigators in the second of the night's two games.

Stark, formerly of the Toronto Blue Jays and a replacement player for the New York Yankees, came off the bench to nail the first pitch in the ninth from Venezuelan relief ace Oscar Henriquez over the centre-field wall and tie the game at 5-5, setting off a wild celebration among Mexican fans at Hermosillo's packed 15,500-seat Hector Espino Stadium.

Later in the inning, Oscar Romero had the game-winner when his sacrifice fly drove in Darryl Brinkley, the Most Valuable Player last year when Mexico won the Caribbean Series. Brinkley had singled, advanced on an infield single and stolen third.

Venezuela's Bob Abreu was nearly the game's hero after he cranked a two-run homer in the eighth inning to give Venezuela a 5-4 advantage. Luis Raven had a solo homer in the inning as the Venezuelans came back from a 4-1 deficit.
In the first game, the Dominican Republic blasted out 14 hits including four home runs to rout Puerto Rico.
The Dominican Republic, represented by Aguilas Cibaenas, jumped ahead in the top of the first inning with four hits and four runs. They were helped by two Puerto Rican errors.
The Dominicans got home runs from Guillermo Garcia, Tony Batista, Luis Polonia and Miguel Tejado.

Puerto Rico, represented by the Mayaguez Indians, got a solo homer from Pedro Munoz in the second inning and rallied in the ninth with a one-run shot by Jose Hernandez and a two-run homer by Eduardo Guzman.

Should the series end in a two-way tie at the conclusion of Sunday's games, a one-game playoff will be held Sunday night. Series officials will meet ahead of Sunday's games to decide what to do in the event of a four-way tie.
